You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository sympy/sympy.

Problem Statement:
Title: Incomplete Coordinate List Now Triggers Error Instead of Auto-Filling Missing Coordinates

Description:
With the recent changes, the gap filling behavior in coordinate generation has been removed. When supplying an incomplete list of generalized coordinates (for example, providing only 2 coordinates for a 3-coordinate joint), the function now raises a ValueError instead of auto-filling the missing coordinate. This behavior change affects cases where the user might expect the missing coordinates to be generated automatically.

Below is a simplified example that reproduces the issue:

```
from sympy.physics.mechanics import PinJoint, _generate_body
from sympy import symbols, Matrix

# Create symbolic generalized coordinates
q0, q1, q2 = symbols('q0 q1 q2')

# Generate body frames (details omitted)
_, _, P, C = _generate_body()

# Instantiate a joint and try to fill coordinates with an incomplete list
joint = PinJoint('J', P, C)
# Attempt to provide only two coordinates while three are required
print(joint._fill_coordinate_list([q0, q1], 3))
```

Expected Behavior:
Providing an incomplete coordinate list should signal an error by raising a ValueError indicating the mismatch (e.g., "Expected 3 qs, instead got 2 qs"), ensuring that users explicitly supply all required coordinates.

Actual Behavior:
Before this change, missing values were automatically filled, which could lead to ambiguous or unexpected joint definitions. The removal of gap filling now causes the function to raise an error in these cases, which may break tests or workflows relying on the old behavior.

Additional Context:
Similar behavior adjustments were observed in spherical joint coordinate generation, where an incomplete set of coordinates now correctly results in a ValueError. This change is intended to enforce explicit and unambiguous specification of joint coordinates.

entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Root cause: `Joint._fill_coordinate_list` in `sympy/physics/mechanics/joint.py` had a loop that auto-generated dynamicsymbols for any missing coordinates when a non-empty but incomplete list was supplied, allowing ambiguous joint definitions. Fix: removed the gap-filling loop so incomplete lists now raise `ValueError` with the message "Expected {n} qs, instead got {m} qs" (using the `label`, q/u), while auto-generation is still performed when no coordinates are supplied at all (`None` or an empty list), and `None` entries within a full-length list are still generated. This affects all joints (Pin, Prismatic, Cylindrical, Planar, Spherical) since they all use this helper; the 3 pre-existing tests encoding the old auto-fill behavior fail as expected by the issue.
